prompt: Which of these is a valid pre-trade checklist item?

options.text: I can judge the setup at the moment
Is the stop price written in my plan before entry? Yes or no.
The setup looks strong
I feel confident about this trade

explanations.a: Judging at the moment is the habit a checklist replaces. The item must be checkable before entry, as a yes or no.
explanations.c: "Looks strong" is a feeling, not a yes or no test with evidence.
explanations.d: A feeling of confidence cannot be checked. It is not a checklist item.

prompt: Hypothetical. Entry Rs 250, stop Rs 240, target Rs 275. What is the break-even win rate before costs, in percent? Give one decimal place.
Hypothetical. A setup has R = 1, so the break-even win rate before costs is 50%. Someone says: "A 1:1 setup with a 60% win rate is always good." Which correction is right?

options.text: Yes, always, because 60% is more than 50%
No. 60% is above the 50% break-even before costs, but a few trades do not prove it, and costs are not yet included
No, because 1:1 setups never work
Yes, because costs do not matter

explanations.a: Being above break-even before costs does not make a setup always good. The result depends on costs and on how many trades show it.
explanations.c: The arithmetic does not say that. A 1:1 setup needs 50% before costs, and it can still lose if the win rate is lower.
explanations.d: Costs reduce what you keep. They matter a great deal for small trades.

prompt: Hypothetical. A setup passes four checklist items and fails two. Your plan says any failed item means no trade. What should you do?

options.text: Trade it, because four of six is most of the list
Do not trade it, because the plan says a failed item means no trade
Trade a smaller size to test the setup
Change the checklist so the setup passes

explanations.a: The plan rule is about failed items, not the share that passed. The plan says no trade.
explanations.c: A smaller size is still a trade. The plan says a failed item means no trade.
explanations.d: Changing the checklist to fit the setup defeats the plan. Plan changes belong in a new version, made before the next setup.

prompt: Hypothetical. You did not trade today, and you think: "Not trading means I am behind." Which response is correct?

options.text: Correct, because every day needs a trade
Wrong. No trade is a valid outcome of the plan
Correct, because I am missing gains
Correct only for beginners

explanations.a: No plan requires a trade every day. A day with no trade can be the right result.
explanations.c: Missing a trade is not a loss to the plan. The plan allows no-trade days.
explanations.d: No-trade days are part of the plan for every level of trader.

prompt: Hypothetical plan line: "Trade when it looks strong." Which part of this line is the mistake?

options.text: Writing a plan at all
"Looks strong" is a feeling, not a yes or no test the plan can check
Trading at all
Nothing is wrong, because the line is short

explanations.a: A plan is the right tool. The mistake is in the test the plan uses to decide.
explanations.c: Trading is allowed. The mistake is the test for entering, which cannot be checked.
explanations.d: Short is fine. The line fails because it cannot be checked before entry.
